title: Coordinate sunsetting of adaptive client compatibility shim for legacy streaming and provide client fallback playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: We will retire the adaptive client compatibility shim that translates legacy streaming transports (chunked SSE, long-poll multiplexing) into the Unified Streaming API. The shim was introduced to provide a safety net for older SDKs and on-prem adapters, but it incurs maintenance cost, creates opaque latencies, and complicates rollout logic. This ticket defines the PRD-level scope, acceptance criteria, migration guidance for customers, the staged rollout plan, and the operational telemetry and rollback gates required for safe sunsetting.

Goals: 1) Remove the compat shim from the hosted control plane and Dedicated routing layer; 2) Provide SDK patches, CLI migration helpers, and docs so customers can migrate within the compatibility window; 3) Ensure no customer-facing errors for high-traffic customers by providing automatic fallback lanes and circuit-breaker rules during rollout; 4) Capture telemetry to validate functional parity and detect regressions before final turn-off.

Out of scope: full SDK v3 rewrite, embedding bulk transport changes (handled in separate PM tickets), and automated client rewrites. This ticket focuses on the shim deprecation mechanics, customer communication, migration tooling, and release gating.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Compatibility shim is feature-flagged and can be disabled per-customer in staging and production
A2: SDKs (JS, Python, Go) include migration helpers and a deprecation warning with link to migration docs
A3: Migration CLI available to convert legacy SSE/longpoll clients to the new unified streaming route with sample config and tests
A4: Rollout plan with canary cohort and telemetry gates validated against baseline latency/error SLOs for 2 weeks
A5: Customer support runbook and escalation path published; top 20 customers have migration check-ins scheduled
A6: No P0 customer-impact incidents attributable to shim removal during staged rollout period
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flag implementation and internal validation (1 week) - install per-org toggle and smoke tests in staging
Phase 1: Canary cohort (5% traffic) for low-risk orgs with telemetry gate checks every 48 hours (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Expanded canary (25% traffic) and targeted top-customer dry-runs with opt-in test windows (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 75% with additional automated fallbacks enabled (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Turn-off for new clients by default and scheduled org opt-out windows for legacy customers (1 week)
Phase 5: Complete removal of shim from control plane after sustained 30-day gate success and customer confirmations
rollback_criteria: If error rate attributable to shim disable increases by >50% relative to baseline for a cohort, rollback to previous toggled state for that cohort
If 95th percentile token latency increases by >100ms for >10% of requests during a 24 hour window, pause rollout and revert for impacted orgs
If two or more customer escalations with reproducible data occur inside the canary window, stop ramp and engage on-call engineering and PM
Manual abort allowed by PM + Eng Lead + SRE if instrumentation indicates any data loss during translation
telemetry_gates: Functional: parity of streamed event shapes (event type counts, end-of-stream markers) between shim-on and shim-off cohorts
Reliability: sustained error rate <= baseline + 0.5% for cohort windows
Performance: median token latency delta <= 40ms and 95th percentile delta <= 100ms
Operational: no backlog growth in the serving runtime's batching queue beyond historical variance
Quality: downstream client integration tests (sampled SDK runners) show parity in 99/100 sampled prompts
